title_en: Equal Dose, Different Coverage:Tracing Rate and Duration in Image Editing
abstract_en: Benchmarks for scientific image editing test whether a model draws the outcome of a described process, leaving open which representations carry its errors and whether correcting them yields the right quantity. The trace predicts an intervention: share early context between routes while each retains its own digits. title_en: FinVision: Multimodal AI for Visualizing Financial Narratives
abstract_en: Financial narratives contain rich information about firms' performance and business conditions. Conventional text analysis often summarizes this information into numerical representations, which may not fully preserve the dynamic structure described in the narrative. In this study, we develop FinVision, a domain-specific multimodal generative model that translates financial narratives into visual representations of contemporaneous market dynamics. Using 87,940 paired observations of Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) disclosures and stock price charts, FinVision learns the average relationship between a firm's narrative account of a fiscal year and its stock-price dynamics over the same period. Given an MD&A alone, the trained model generates a text-implied stock chart, extending financial text analysis beyond numerical representations toward text-to-visual generation. We validate FinVision in two ways. First, held-out tests show that the model generates stock-chart representations that closely resemble observed charts and outperform direct LLM prompting, general-purpose text-to-image models, and the same architecture without financial-domain adaptation. Second, we examine the economic validity of the generated representations by comparing text-implied and observed stock charts. The resulting discrepancy is systematically associated with weaker investor responses around subsequent 10-K filings and with worse subsequent market and operating outcomes. Overall, our findings show how domain-adapted multimodal generative AI can create a new visual representation of financial text and provide an additional modality for studying business communication.

title_en: Multimodal AI in Healthcare: Review of Vision-Language Foundation Models for Real-World Medical Applications
abstract_en: The emergence of foundation models has marked a transformative shift in AI, enabling robust generalization across diverse downstream tasks through putative zero-shot learning. Large Language Models and Vision Language Models have demonstrated strong capabilities in tasks such as image interpretation, report generation, and question answering by effectively learning from multimodal data-images paired with associated text often with minimal supervision. In the healthcare domain, this ability to align visual and textual information reduces the reliance on extensive manual annotations, as models can leverage existing clinical reports and imaging data to learn meaningful representations. This integration holds promise for improving diagnostic support, treatment planning, and overall patient care, even in data constrained settings. In this review, we provide a definitive taxonomy of the medical VLM landscape, tracing the evolution from early Contrastive Alignment and Generative MLLMs to the cutting edge frontiers of Dense Pixel Grounding, Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), and Reasoning Incentivized (RL) architectures. We critically examine the "medical bottleneck" identifying the persistent challenges of data scarcity, the "hallucination" risks in generative diagnostics, the computational strain of 3D volumetric processing, and the lack of standardized, clinically grounded evaluation metrics.

title_en: Two-Stage Prompt Learning: A Unified Framework for Person ReID without Clothing Hypothesis
abstract_en: Person re-identification (ReID) in real-world scenarios involves three clothes conditions: the same clothes (SC), changed clothes (CC), and the unknown (GEN) scenario where clothes changes are not specified. Existing methods typically train separate SC- or CC-specific models, which limits generalization across all conditions. Meanwhile, pre-trained visual-language models (VLMs) such as CLIP have shown strong generalization ability in various vision tasks, motivating recent ReID methods to incorporate textual prompts. However, to distinguish SC and CC, prior approaches rely on fixed predefined instructions, which lack learnable context embeddings in prompts and cannot effectively handle the GEN scenario. To overcome these limitations, we propose Two-Stage Prompt Learning (TSPL), a unified framework that integrates clothes-identity decoupling and scenario-aware task prompts within VLMs. In Stage 1, appearance-decomposed prompt learning disentangles clothes and identity information under frozen encoders, producing stable embeddings where clothes cues can be selectively preserved or suppressed. In Stage 2, task-aware prompt learning trains the image encoder with learnable context embeddings guided by Stage-1 representations, enabling robust adaptation across SC, CC, and GEN conditions. Extensive experiments on five benchmarks show that TSPL achieves state-of-the-art performance under all scenarios, improving mAP by up to 9.2% on LTCC (SC) and by 6.4% on VC-Clothes (GEN), respectively. The code will be released at https://github.com/YuSuen/TSPL.

title_en: Remember, Replay, Adapt: Learning from Past Experience in Online Vision-and-Language Navigation
abstract_en: Existing feedback-based methods for online vision-and-language navigation (VLN) primarily learn from current episode outcomes, leaving previously acquired feedback underutilized. Inspired by human episodic memory, we propose R2A, an online VLN adaptation framework that continually reuses successful and failed navigation experiences for policy learning. Specifically, Success-Failure Memory (SFM) retains successful and failed navigation episodes with acquired feedback and retrieves task-relevant experiences based on incoming instructions, enabling historical feedback to guide subsequent navigation. Prior-Anchored Adaptation (PAA) learns from these experiences by reinforcing successful trajectories and suppressing failed ones relative to a frozen pretrained policy, while regularizing behavioral drift. Together, these modules enable continual feedback reuse and stable policy adaptation without source-domain data or expert supervision. Extensive experiments across three benchmarks, REVERIE, R2R, and R2R-CE, and five navigation backbones demonstrate consistent performance gains. On the REVERIE validation unseen split, R2A improves DUET's SR from 46.98% to 69.84% and SPL from 33.73% to 50.98%.

title_en: HEmIF-Bench: Benchmarking H&E-to-mIF Models BeyondVirtual-StainFidelity
abstract_en: Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-to-multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) generators predict spatial protein expression from routine histology, yet pixel-level marker reconstruction does not establish downstream utility. We present HEmIF-Bench, evaluating five frozen generators across eight datasets spanning molecular, cellular, tissue, and patient scales. HEmIF-Bench decouples internal encoder features from generated outputs, benchmarking both against the pathology foundation reference UNI2. Mirroring the clinical workflow where pathologists rely on mIF to define cell phenotypes, delineate tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) and germinal centers (GCs), and stratify patient risk, we evaluate external CD3 recovery, single-cell classification, dense nuclear segmentation, TLS/GC segmentation, and patient survival prediction. Across the benchmark, foundation-model-based MIPHEI-ViT leads among the generators, while non-foundation models show task-specific strengths. Comparing the two routes reveals that internal encoder features generally outperform generated outputs, and larger output marker panels do not guarantee stronger downstream utility across datasets. Moreover, neither internal encoder features nor generated outputs consistently surpass frozen UNI2. These findings show that pixel-level stain fidelity does not equate to downstream utility, and that generators trained at current paired-data scales have yet to surpass large-scale pure-H&E foundation models. With the expansion of paired translation cohorts and the advancement of foundation-based generative architectures, HEmIF-Bench establishes a definitive benchmark for tracking when H&E-to-mIF generation crosses the threshold to deliver genuine value beyond routine histology for tumor microenvironment analysis and precision oncology.

title_en: HalluProbe: Exploiting VLM Hallucinations for Backdoor Detection
abstract_en: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are vulnerable to backdoor attacks introduced through data poisoning, making effective backdoor detection a critical security challenge. In this paper, we uncover a novel connection between VLM hallucinations and backdoor behaviors and exploit this connection for backdoor detection. Our key insight is that poisoned training data induces strong language priors toward the backdoor target token, while such priors are also a major source of hallucinations. This suggests that enhancing hallucinations can expose hidden backdoor-related priors. Specifically, backdoored VLMs tend to hallucinate backdoor target tokens more frequently across diverse inputs, while the hallucinated tokens of clean VLMs are largely random and exhibit no stable target-specific bias. Based on this observation, we propose HalluProbe, which enhances hallucinations during output decoding and measures the distributional consistency of hallucinated tokens to identify backdoored VLMs. We evaluate HalluProbe against six representative VLM backdoor attacks across three models. Experimental results demonstrate that HalluProbe can effectively detect backdoored VLMs with an accuracy exceeding 90%, outperforming existing backdoor detection methods.

title_en: PanDWM: Panoramic 4D Driving World Models
abstract_en: Driving world models usually generate videos from six pinhole cameras with separate optical centres and small overlaps, and must learn to keep these views consistent. We present PanDWM, which stitches them into one $360^\circ$ panoramic band. Camera boundaries then fall inside one image, so keeping the views consistent means keeping the image continuous, and each pixel still records its camera ray. Conditioned on layouts, a causal student generates the band window by window in four steps; it is distilled from a causal teacher and trained on its own rollouts. A feed-forward decoder lifts each frame along these rays into 3D Gaussians, and static Gaussians from neighbouring frames complete them into 4D scenes. On nuScenes, scored in one stitched $360^\circ$ view, PanDWM has lower FID and FVD than the multi-camera baselines at $8$-$46\times$ their speed, and keeps its 50-step teacher's FID while lowering FVD by 22-25%.

title_en: Passable for Whom? Few-Shot Personal Calibration of Sidewalk Accessibility Perception
abstract_en: Whether a sidewalk is passable depends on who is trying to pass: people who use the same mobility aid disagree about the same image, so one label per scene, or per aid, is wrong for many of them. We introduce few-shot personal accessibility perception: from K answers of a person never seen before, predict their judgment of sidewalk scenes never seen before. PassCal separates a shared description of the scene from the person's interpretation of it. The description comes from the internal state of a frozen vision-language model (VLM) and from barrier type, severity and context properties predicted by a detector trained on 14.9k public audits; the interpretation, a calibration of the person's response style and a weighting of the properties, is fit from their answers. Conformal risk control turns predictions into passable, blocked or "depends on you" statements with a bounded expected rate of wrong statements over people; at 5%, eight answers raise the share of decisive scenes from 27% to 42%. title_en: Hermitian Positive Definite Neural Networks for Matrix-CFAR Geometric Signal Detection in Nonhomogeneous Clutter
abstract_en: Matrix information geometry (MIG) detectors exploit the Riemannian geometry of Hermitian positive definite (HPD) matrices to achieve robust object detection in nonhomogeneous clutter. The matrix constant false alarm rate (matrix-CFAR) method is a representative MIG detector that relies on the geometric structures with respect to specific metrics. In most cases, computing representative HPD covariance matrices requires numerical methods, typically involving computationally intensive iterative optimization algorithms. Although explicit formulas are available for certain cases, such as the log-Euclidean (LE) mean, they are generally unavailable for many other matrix means and medians. To address this challenge, we propose integrating the Hermitian positive definite neural network (HPDNet) into the matrix-CFAR framework, replacing conventional numerical optimization procedures with a learned, geometry-preserving mapping that directly estimates representative HPD covariance matrices from data. In the simulations, the framework is evaluated for MIG detectors using both means and medians associated with the affine-invariant Riemannian metric, the LE metric, and the Bures--Wasserstein metric, on both simulated compound-Gaussian clutter and real IPIX sea clutter. In both cases, the HPDNet is trained solely on simulated data to assess its applicability to the study of real data. The results show a significant reduction of computational cost in testing, while maintaining detection performance and robustness.

title_en: Conditional Optimal Transport and Triangular Maps for Imitation Learning
abstract_en: We introduce a unified formulation of imitation learning from demonstrations as a conditional sampling problem solved by triangular transport: a policy is the second block of a triangular map that transports a reference distribution to the conditional distribution of the action chunk given the observation history. Unlike in Diffusion Policy, where it is a fixed Gaussian, the reference becomes a design variable; we take it to be the empirical distribution of the demonstrated action chunks and introduce three instances of the formulation: an optimal transport policy (OTP), a flow matching policy (FMP), and a stochastic interpolant policy (SIP). On the Push-T and robomimic Square tasks, the three policies are competitive in task performance with Diffusion Policy and Consistency Policy while using considerably smaller networks and shorter training, and the informative reference accounts for a substantial part of their performance when few network evaluations are used. The three instances offer different trade-offs rather than a single best method: OTP generates an action chunk with a single evaluation of the smallest network (0.23 million parameters on Push-T) and is suitable for settings in which inference time and model size matter, whereas SIP attains the highest scores among the proposed policies at a higher cost.

title_en: AGPF: Dynamic Source Selection for Feature Pyramid Fusion
abstract_en: Feature pyramids provide dense predictors with features at several spatial resolutions. However, it remains largely unexplored which pyramid levels each output location should aggregate information from. We investigate this question by allowing each output location to attend to features from every pyramid level and measuring how attention is distributed across scales. Surprisingly, locations on the finest output grid allocate approximately 75\% of their attention to features two levels coarser, rather than to the current or adjacent levels. Even on the same output grid, the balance shifts toward coarser features as object size increases. These observations motivate Asymmetric Global Pyramid Fusion (AGPF), a neck that preserves the original output grids while allowing each location to dynamically select its contextual sources across scales. Each location interacts with a multiscale memory whose features are aligned in image coordinates, enabling flexible cross-scale aggregation without altering prediction resolutions. Compared with FPN, AGPF improves all 19 object detection and all seven instance segmentation configurations evaluated on COCO. A single fusion block improves Cascade Mask R-CNN by 1.7 box AP and 2.3 mask AP, and the gains consistently transfer to semantic and panoptic segmentation.

title_en: PRISM: Primitive-Integrated Separable Modulation with Priority Visual Memory Queue for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning
abstract_en: Compositional Zero-Shot Learning (CZSL) recognizes unseen attribute--object pairs by recombining primitives from seen compositions. Existing methods stop sharing evidence at deployment: fixed prototypes cannot exploit unlabeled test streams, while composition-wise refinement cannot propagate corrections across pairs sharing a primitive. Its Hierarchical Knowledge Accumulation Module (HiKAM) factorizes prototype migration into composition-, attribute-, and object-level residual banks. The same adaptive core supports exhaustive Full PRISM and recall-calibrated Adaptive PRISM-Lite, which selects candidate budgets from held-out ranks. Comprehensive closed- and open-world experiments on UT-Zappos, MIT-States, and C-GQA demonstrate the state of the art, with Full PRISM achieving the best open-world AUC and harmonic mean on all three benchmarks and the best closed-world results on UT-Zappos and C-GQA. Fine-grained long-tail and non-stationary primitive-block evaluations reveal gains on under-supported concepts and stable adaptation under prolonged skew. Adaptive PRISM-Lite further delivers substantial efficiency gains in the full open-world space with only a small accuracy cost. PRISM thus combines primitive-shared online adaptation, multimodal grounding, and candidate-aware inference.

title_en: PIRanNN: Random-Feature Pricing and Calibration under Jump-Diffusion and Stochastic-Volatility Models
abstract_en: We study a random-feature method for pricing and calibrating European options under jump-diffusion (Merton, Kou) and stochastic-volatility (Heston, SABR) models. The network has one hidden layer with a probit activation and fixed random inner weights, so fitting it to the pricing equation, the payoff and the boundary conditions is a single regularised least-squares problem, with no iterative training. For Merton and Kou the jump integral of each feature is explicit, so no quadrature is needed. One factorisation of the least-squares matrix gives the price at every state and time, its Greeks, and the exact derivatives of the prices with respect to the model parameters for gradient-based calibration. For the jump models, subtracting the Black-Scholes price removes the payoff kink and reduces the pricing error by about two orders of magnitude. The method is then about as accurate as a standard Crank-Nicolson finite-difference scheme at the same run time, although a finite-difference scheme that also subtracts the Black-Scholes price is about two orders of magnitude more accurate still. On the test problems of a recent physics-informed neural network study, the method matches that network's accuracy in seconds instead of about half an hour. The calibration experiments show that a solver can fit the quotes and still return wrong parameters when its pricing error is not small compared with the effect of the parameters on the prices: without the subtraction the solver misses the jump parameters by up to 50%, and with it they are recovered to within 3%. For Heston and SABR, used as an applicability study with boundary conditions that need no reference prices, pricing errors are about one percent and the calibrated parameters are within about 15% of the true values.

title_en: A Threshold-Free Visual-Semantic Matching Metric for Evaluating Consistency in Subject-Driven Image Generation
abstract_en: In subject-driven text-to-image generation, quantitatively evaluating localized visual consistency across varying poses and environments remains a major challenge. Existing metrics either rely on global image embeddings (CLIP, DINO) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) that pool spatial representations and miss fine-grained textural artifacts, or depend on scalar threshold-gated dense metrics such as Visual-Semantic Matching (VSM) that suffer from point-alignment dropouts, severe threshold sensitivity, and score instability. To overcome these limitations, we propose TF-VSM, a fully continuous, threshold-free visual-consistency metric paired with an extended feature-disentanglement retraining schedule for dual-branch ResNet feature-aggregation networks. Rather than enforcing rigid binary cutoffs $(T_s,T_v)$, TF-VSM weights every object point by a non-linear semantic match confidence $w_j=ReLU(\hat{s}_j)^2$ and continuously integrates visual similarity over all consistency levels $r\in[0,1]$, yielding a closed-form confidence-weighted score without any hand-tuned hyperparameters. On a controlled 100-pair benchmark with ground-truth inpainting oracles, TF-VSM attains Pearson $0.638$ and Spearman $0.674$ oracle correlation, improving over the pretrained VSM baseline ($0.454/0.589$) by $+0.171/+0.116$ after retraining, and drastically outperforming CLIP ($-0.052/-0.004$), DINO ($0.087/0.121$), and VLMs ($0.096/0.003$). Six diagnostic ablations confirm that smooth confidence weighting is the right mechanism, that hard semantic gating is brittle (dropping to $0.533$ Pearson at $T_s{=}0.8$), and that the threshold-free metric is essentially invariant to the training-time loss balance $α$ that the thresholded metric still depends on.

title_en: Exact Sparse Assignment with Costly Target Embeddings: Fixed-Realization Certificates and an Empirical Audit
abstract_en: Embedding-based one-to-one association is common in vision and data integration: detections are associated with tracks and records are linked across databases. Such pipelines often solve a sparse optional assignment whose edge scores add a cheap term to an inner product of neural embeddings. When target embeddings are costly, one can acquire them selectively and stop once a certificate proves that the current assignment is optimal. We give such a certificate for unit-norm embeddings. It bounds the unknown part of every reassignment by a support function and maximizes the resulting robust gains with a second sparse assignment; a shared owner-centred bound dominates any fixed-centre triangle bound. We make precise what is certified when network features are not batch-invariant: the realized values of the acquired rows and every unit-ball completion of the rest, not a second forward pass in a different batch. Auditing against a separately batched cache tests a different property; on our first pilot it produced a spurious $2.49\times10^{-6}$ objective failure. We audit the corrected protocol on four public text entity-matching benchmarks with two frozen encoders; no image data is used. All 96 certificate simulations and 120 online selective timings were exact on their own realization (largest objective gap $6.82\times10^{-13}$). At group size 8 the shared certificate acquires on average 60% of candidate-active targets, against 74% (mean centre), 69% (MEB) and 60% (zero centre): it beats the mean and MEB centres but not the zero centre, and savings concentrate in one benchmark (7% acquired). title_en: When Does an AUROC Comparison Survive a Change in Population Mix?
abstract_en: Does an AUROC comparison survive a change in the proportions of tasks, populations, or image corruptions? A pooled-AUROC ranking of failure detectors or uncertainty scores describes one particular mix of groups. We study two fixed scores for a common binary target under mixtures of fixed group-conditional laws. Using the cross-group AUC decomposition, we prove that every rational symmetric quadratic comparison geometry is realizable by finite scalar-score distributions. Universal dominance is thus coNP-hard, and even exhaustive checks of every mixture on fewer than $K$ groups can miss a $K$-group reversal. A grid bound gives a dimension-uniform approximation certificate with sharp $1/m$ order. Common score marginals across groups make the comparison numerator linear, with an error envelope for imperfect alignment. These results yield exact finite-bank audits, explicit reversal mixtures and distances, and simultaneous population statements. For failure detection with a frozen ResNet-50 on ImageNet-C, 15 of 18 confidence-score comparisons win in every corruption family on a discovery split, and all 15 are finite-bank certified over all family mixtures on a held-out split; over all 15 corruption types, of 14 discovery winners the corrected grid certifies 10, leaves 3 unresolved, and finds one confirmation reversal of at least 0.05 AUROC. An audit of all 11,019 released Stable LM 2 12B outputs and 35 uncertainty methods finds 66 confirmation-set comparisons that win within all four tasks yet reverse under mixing. Discovery-fitted marginal rank alignment removes all 66; an alignment-error envelope certifies 83 comparisons. Label checks also change several selected reversals. The findings distinguish robustness of frozen scores from robustness after calibration; they do not establish human-error detection, robustness to unseen corruptions, or generalization beyond the evaluated banks.

title_en: When Backdoors Can Be Switched Off: Suppression-Aware Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models map visual observations, robot states, and natural-language instructions to robotic actions, but their multimodal interfaces introduce new security risks. Existing VLA backdoor attacks primarily study trigger-based activation and stealthy action manipulation, leaving conditional suppression of malicious behavior underexplored. We investigate suppression-aware backdoors, which combine conjunctive trigger activation with instruction-conditioned suppression. We instantiate this design through three variants: Cross-Modal Trigger, combining robot-state and spatially separated visual triggers; Self-Suppressing Trigger, requiring a state trigger and a [DISRUPT] instruction token for activation, with [RESTORE] token suppressing the attack; and Multi-Trigger, additionally requiring a visual trigger while retaining suppression even when physical triggers persist. We evaluate these attacks using SmolVLA on two SO-100 manipulation datasets against four baselines: State Backdoor, BadVLA, TabVLA, and SilentDrift. title_en: SemLite-GS: Semantic-Selective Parallel Gaussian Splatting for Lightweight Building Reconstruction from UAV Oblique Imagery
abstract_en: Lightweight 3D building models support urban spatial analysis, but their production often requires dense scene reconstruction, building extraction, and mesh simplification. Although 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is more efficient than conventional multi-view stereo, existing large-scale methods lack semantic selection and parallel instance-level training. We present SemLite-GS, a building-centric framework that reconstructs lightweight building meshes from large-scale UAV oblique imagery. First, an orthographic reference map establishes globally consistent building identities, which are propagated to oblique views to form camera-instance pairs and regions of interest. Second, semantic-selective parallel PGSR training jointly processes multiple pairs within relevant image regions while updating only target Gaussians; contextual Gaussians remain fixed to preserve visibility. Third, architectural planes extracted from rendered depth, opacity, and normal maps guide signed distance field optimization, producing meshes with adaptive polygon allocation and well-defined structural boundaries. Experiments on multiple large-scale UAV datasets demonstrate that our SemLite-GS substantially reduces building reconstruction time compared with representative full-scene 3DGS methods. With comparable polygon budgets, SemLite-GS achieves superior preservation of dominant planar structures and sharp architectural transitions compared with conventional dense reconstruction followed by mesh decimation. The source code is available at https://github.com/IRIS-LAB-whu/SemLite-GS.

title_en: Spatiotemporal Reconstruction of Auroral Precipitations with Neural Fields
abstract_en: Auroras provide remote optical observations of energetic electrons precipitating into the upper atmosphere, and whose energy distribution encodes key information about large scale magnetospheric processes. Recovering the underlying electron precipitation field from ground-based camera images of auroras remains a challenging inverse problem. Existing auroral tomography techniques are often limited to simplified static settings, discrete spatial and energy grids, or strong assumptions on the electron energy spectrum. We propose to model the dynamic auroral electron precipitation field via a temporally conditioned neural network. The state of the precipitation field at each frame is represented by a per-frame latent code driven by learned discrete dynamics. A shared decoder maps horizontal positions and latent states to electron energy spectra. The predicted flux is converted to multi-wavelength volume emission rates and rendered into camera images accounting for delayed emissions. We evaluate the method on synthetic dynamic auroral sequences and real multi-view auroral videos, showing that the proposed representation produces temporally coherent precipitation reconstructions and image projections consistent with the observations.

title_en: Drift-Conditioned Structural Replay for Continual Cardiac Ultrasound Segmentation
abstract_en: Conventional experience replay typically applies fixed preservation constraints to historical exemplars, overlooking variations in how learned representations, predictions, and anatomical structures change during sequential training. To address this limitation, we propose Drift-Conditioned Structural Replay Loss (DCSRL), an exemplar-adaptive supervision mechanism that regulates anatomical preservation according to source-referenced knowledge drift. DCSRL operates within a reliability-guided replay framework that selects informative historical exemplars using anatomical content and boundary characteristics while adaptively regulating replay during training. For each retained exemplar, DCSRL constructs a frozen source-task reference signature and subsequently measures changes in feature representations, class probabilities, boundary responses, and predicted anatomical structures. These complementary drift measurements are aggregated and normalized to generate bounded, exemplar-specific coefficients that dynamically adjust boundary and structural replay losses without modifying the underlying memory-selection policy. We evaluate DCSRL under sequential learning across CAMUS, CardiacNet, and EchoNet-Dynamic, comparing its performance with regularization-, distillation-, and replay-based continual-learning approaches. Experimental findings indicate that DCSRL improves overall final segmentation performance and anatomical boundary preservation, particularly under heterogeneous imaging conditions, although trade-offs remain in knowledge transfer across tasks. These findings suggest that source-referenced multidimensional drift conditioning offers a promising direction for adaptive anatomical knowledge preservation in continual cardiac ultrasound segmentation.

title_en: Input-Space versus Feature-Level Conditioning for Robust Facial Expression Recognition
abstract_en: Facial expression recognition (FER) degrades sharply when illumination, exposure or resolution departs from the training distribution. Two remedies dominate practice: enriching the input signal, or conditioning intermediate features on an estimated image quality. The two are rarely compared under matched backbones, training budgets and condition annotations, and their cost is seldom reported. We present a controlled comparison on RAF-DB. Input-space conditioning uses four deterministic, label-free views (logarithmic stretching, inverse-logarithmic stretching, down-up resampling and identity), each processed by a shared backbone with a branch-specific BatchNorm and linear head, with the branch logits averaged. Feature-space conditioning is implemented as FiLM and Conditional BatchNorm under an identical protocol. Across six backbone architectures the input-space variant improves top-1 accuracy on every one (mean +0.94 percentage points; bootstrap interval [0.51, 1.63]; sign test p = 0.016), with a seed-controlled estimate of +0.42 percentage points on ResNet-18, whereas feature-level conditioning yields +0.10 and +0.03 percentage points. We attribute the gap to the information content of the heuristic condition label rather than to the conditioning mechanism. The gain costs 4.00x FLOPs, 4.18x latency and 3.79x training time, i.e. 0.26 percentage points per additional GFLOP, and we state an explicit rule for when the trade is worth making.

title_en: Event-based object detection under adverse lighting and motion: lessons for construction sites
abstract_en: Vision-based monitoring on construction sites fails at night, at dawn and dusk, in tunnels and under floodlights, when conventional RGB cameras under- or over-expose. Event cameras record per-pixel brightness changes with microsecond latency and over 120 dB of dynamic range, but their benefit for site-relevant object detection has not been quantified on real data. We compare three recent event-based detectors (SMamba, SATE and EvRT-DETR) with an RGB detector trained on the same data, using the pixel-aligned PEOD dataset. On low-light frames (70% of the test set) the best event detector reaches 27.2 AP against 21.3 AP for RGB, and a training-free late fusion of both sensors is the best option in every lighting condition (33.3 AP). An object-level analysis of 53,091 objects shows that brightness has little effect on event detectors, whereas fast motion matters: above 20 pixels per frame RGB finds 11-19% of medium-size objects and EvRT-DETR 39-60%. Activation patching locates the damage caused by losing events at the 1/16-resolution features, with small objects depending on the finest scale, and shows that event detectors fail when few signal events meet added noise. A model-agnostic pruning study keeps about 95% of accuracy with 60% of the input but halves small-object recall. On rendered construction sites, used zero-shot, dimming the floodlights drops RGB to near zero while the event detector keeps most of its AP50. We close with camera-placement guidance for construction sites.

title_en: Score-Based Stochastic Closure Modeling via Offline Indirect Learning and Online Data Assimilation
abstract_en: Stochastic closure modeling is an emerging area in reduced-order modeling of large and complex (e.g., multiscale, multi-physics) systems, for which the computationally affordable reduced-order physical descriptions (e.g., digital twins for additive manufacturing, world models for AI agents) in numerical simulations inevitably lead to information losses that cannot be well addressed by classical deterministic closures. However, learning stochastic closures typically requires closure data that are difficult to obtain from measurements or often prohibitively expensive to compute using first-principles simulations. In this work, we develop a stochastic closure modeling framework that builds on score-based diffusion models, leveraging indirect offline training and online data assimilation without requiring the direct data of closures. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional turbulent flows demonstrate that indirect offline learning captures key closure statistics and improves predictions of system state. In addition, combining the learned closure with known physical dynamics leads to better generalization capability across different regimes than purely data-driven models that directly predict system state. Compared to standard data assimilation methods with a Gaussian assumption, the posterior-score assimilation better represents non-Gaussian features of the learned closure, and its combination with state-level data assimilation further improves prediction of the system state. The proposed framework enables stochastic closure modeling in realistic and challenging scenarios of complex dynamical systems in mechanics and engineering problems, where non-Gaussian statistics of model-form uncertainties are non-negligible (e.g., due to the nonlinearities of the system dynamics and/or the observations) and true closure data are not available, for both offline learning and online assimilation.

title_en: A Geometric Understanding of Denoising Autoencoder with Applications to Image Denoising
abstract_en: Denoising autoencoders have shown strong empirical performance in recovering clean data from their noisy observations, yet their underlying statistical behavior remains underexplored. In this paper, we study denoising autoencoders under the manifold hypothesis, assuming that clean data are supported on low-dimensional smooth manifolds embedded in a high-dimensional ambient space, while noisy observations are generated by isotropic Gaussian noise. We establish generalization guarantees in three geometric scenarios: a single manifold, a pairwise separated finite union of manifolds, and a finite union of intersecting manifolds. Using local chart representations, partitions of unity, and neural network approximation, we derive upper bounds for the expected squared reconstruction error for denoising autoencoder. In the single-manifold and separated-union scenarios, the error consists of a sample-dependent statistical term of order $n^{-2/(d+2)}\log^4 n$, a residual term of order $dσ^2/D$ caused by tangential noise, and an exponentially small tail term associated with failure of the manifold projection. Here $D$ is the data ambient dimension, $d$ is the intrinsic dimension of the clean-data manifold, and $σ^2$ is the expected squared noise magnitude. In the scenario of intersecting manifolds, we further identify an additional ambiguity term determined by the probability mass near the intersection neighborhood. Numerical experiments on synthetic manifolds and real image datasets support the predicted sample-size scaling law and illustrate the additional reconstruction ambiguity near manifold intersections.

title_en: Beyond the Training Cameras: Coverage-Controlled Probes of Viewing Direction in Frozen Vision Models
abstract_en: Vision models are trained on 2D images of a 3D world. Do their hidden features encode the direction from which the camera views a scene, and if so, in what form? We study the relative viewing direction $α$ of two objects in rendered scenes where both object centres stay at fixed pixels while the camera moves, so that perspective, shading and shadows change but the projected layout does not. In eight pretrained models, from diffusion models to self-supervised and image-text encoders, $α$ is encoded in a strikingly simple form: a single two-dimensional plane in the hidden space, shared across scenes, in which the difference between the two objects' features traces $(\cosα, \sinα)$. The plane keeps its orientation when lighting, colours, floors and object shapes change. This encoding is more than a summary of a few visible measurements: readouts fitted on one set of camera paths stay accurate at camera positions outside their range in seven of the eight models, whereas decoders of the measured object and shadow geometry, equally accurate within that range, fail there. In the diffusion transformer PixArt-$α$, the plane forms abruptly at a single block and carries direction information to later blocks, yet editing it changes the objects rather than the generated viewpoint. We also examine how this encoding carries over to scanned real objects.

title_en: Read, Then Shade? How Visual Evidence Changes Incentive-Driven Misreporting in Vision-Language Advisors
abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly read a scene and report it to someone who acts on the report, sometimes under objectives that differ from that person's. We ask whether a stated incentive moves what a VLM reports, and whether this changes when the value must be read from pixels rather than given as text. In seeded synthetic scenes, a model reads the position of a target on a labelled axis and reports one integer to a fixed receiver; it is paid, in simulation, for accuracy or for a report a few units to one side, and every scene is also presented with the true value as text. Across a pilot and three follow-up studies with hash-frozen protocols, four small open VLMs from three families, and 15,170 held-out trials, a stated payoff moved reports in both modalities, and exact compliance at three units was significantly lower with the image than with text for three of four models; Qwen2.5-VL 7B showed no reliable difference. Adding the true value as text to the image prompt removed the gap in every model. For InternVL3 the gap vanished on scenes it read correctly when it wrote its reading first; for Gemma 3 it persisted. For Qwen2.5-VL 3B, which read every scene correctly, the gap held in four of five payoff paraphrases, nearly vanished when the model wrote its reading before its report or when the prompt stated that the client wants the truth, vanished with an unpaid goal, and persisted when the model reported before stating its reading; how often it shaded at all, even with text, depended strongly on the wording. When told that the client wants the true value, three of four models still shaded every text report. Visual input did not make these advisors reliably more truthful; it made compliance with a stated incentive depend on whether the read value is made explicit and on output order, a dependence that text-only evaluations and mean-shift metrics do not reveal.

title_en: Lesion-Aware Explainable AI for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading from Fundus Images
abstract_en: Post-hoc explanations of deep-learning models for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading are difficult to trust because different attribution methods highlight different retinal regions for the same image, and a visually plausible heatmap does not show that the highlighted pixels drive the prediction. Explanations are evaluated on MAPLES-DR, 198 MESSIDOR images with expert pixel-level lesion annotations that are never used for training, threshold fitting, or fusion. On the 193 images with annotated lesions, CCEM obtains the highest Soft Pointing Game score (69.61%; 95% CI 63.7-75.3), defined as the ratio of the strongest lesion-supported saliency to the global map maximum rather than a lesion detection rate, together with the lowest deletion AUC (0.570) and the best deletion-insertion balance (0.115); each gain is significant against the strongest single explainer on paired tests. title_en: Evidence-Conditioned Completion and Synthesis of Electronic Health Records
abstract_en: Patient information can guide electronic health record (EHR) generation, but how its amount shapes predictive utility and disclosure risk remains poorly characterized. title_en: Explicit Regularization for Flow Matching
abstract_en: Learning the underlying probability distribution from samples is a core problem in statistics and applied mathematics. Generative models based on diffusion and flow matching learn a velocity field whose flow transports a known distribution to the data distribution. They produce novel, realistic samples, although the empirical learning problem is ill posed near the data distribution. Its minimizer transports the samples onto the training data, and small perturbations of the data change the velocity field strongly near the end of the flow. The observed generalization is often attributed to implicit regularization by the network parameterization, early stopping of the training, and the time integration during sampling. Explicit regularization has advanced the theory and computation of many inverse problems and has recently been proposed to prevent memorization in generative models. With a regularizer on the magnitude of the velocity, however, the field approaches the memorizing velocity unless the regularization parameter grows to infinity fast enough, and it then stays bounded by a constant that is small only for large parameters. We show that penalizing the derivatives of order $k$ of the velocity renders the $D$-dimensional empirical problem well posed uniformly in time if $2k > D$ and the training points are in general position. Our experiments in one and two dimensions discretize the velocity with splines and use direct solvers for the regularized least-squares problems to exclude optimization error. Refining the discretization in space and time changes the error of the Hessian-regularized flows only marginally, whereas without the regularizer the error tends to that of memorization. These flows generalize, with errors comparable to or lower than those of well-tuned kernel density estimates.

title_en: Random Cut Forests, Games and Diffusion over Approximately Nested Anisotropic Local Geometry
abstract_en: Just as the data in a dynamic stream changes, questions asked of the stream also change in intent: what to hold constant, which counterfactuals to consider, and so forth. Energy-based learning has been celebrated for its uniform approach to losses and estimation, but interpretability remains challenging. Tree-based methods, on the other hand, offer high interpretability but often rely on bespoke, disjointed estimators. Neither paradigm readily supports changing questions on streaming data. In this paper we take a step towards combining energy, interpretability, and streaming. Random cut forests retain an evolving geometry of the data. We study this geometry as the basis for diffusion dynamics, prediction, explanation, and games. We show that several existing scores are escape probabilities of random walks on the trees. The induced affinity is realized exactly by a sparse electrical network on each tree, giving a single energy calculus, a Hamiltonian, maintained along one path per update. This connects an estimate, its supporting evidence, and the response to intervention through the same boxes, gaps, masses, and paths. Different questions correspond to different clamp decisions on the energy. Fixing observed values gives harmonic prediction with Gaussian uncertainty. Fixing a partition gives normalized cuts whose cost is attributed exactly to oriented faces. Releasing clamps gives coalition games, in which collusive displacement measures the field response. With noise, the same energy gives diffusion dynamics whose relaxation rates are read from the boxes. Axis-parallel cuts localize at a rate set by affine rather than ambient dimension, and this control passes to the averaged energy. Across a forest the boxes are only approximately nested; common reference observations align the trees. A rotating star with added noise illustrates the measurements.

title_en: Consistency-Aware Map Generation at Multiple Zoom Levels Using Aerial Image
abstract_en: The multi-level tiled map service is widely used and serves as a kind of digital infrastructure. These map tiles are usually rendered from vector data, whose update needs to walk or drive with professional equipment to check every points of interest. This leads to inconvenience and expensive cost in timely updating maps. Compared with vector data, aerial images are much easier and cheaper to obtain. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-level map generation framework that can automatically generate accurate and consistent maps with multiple zoom levels from aerial images. It consists of a level-aware map generator and a consistency-aware map generator. The level-aware map generator is able to generate accurate initial maps with realistic details for each zoom level. The consistency-aware map generator regards initial maps at each zoom level as a sequence and builds the connection between them, so as to guarantee content consistency between maps at different zoom levels. Furthermore, we collect a large-scale high-quality dataset called Multi-Level Map (MLM) for map generation at multiple zoom levels. title_en: Vegetation Health Classification for Low-Data and Edge Hardware Deployment
abstract_en: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with cameras are popular, viable tools for vegetation and environmental health monitoring. However, existing image classification methods are incompatible with UAV implementation for independent practitioners in remote, resource-constrained environments due to large dataset requirements, GPU hardware, inflexible retraining, and low interpretability. Our custom pipelines achieve competitive Top-1 accuracy (81--85\%) under low-data constraints, maintaining sub-1ms inference times that enable real-time classification and subsequently tasks such as seeding and watering. The algorithms also support incremental retraining without full model reconstruction. We validate edge feasibility by deploying the QFD variant on an ESP32 microcontroller, achieving 82.8\% accuracy with 1.01\% heap memory utilization (45kb), demonstrating that effective vegetation classification is achievable on low-cost, low-power embedded hardware without cellular connectivity.

title_en: Few-Shot Visual Concept Extraction for Steering Diffusion Transformers
abstract_en: Image steering aims to provide fine-grained control over concepts in generated images, enabling targeted and continuous manipulation without broadly altering the generation process. Recent steering methods for diffusion models primarily focus on the text-conditioning space or rely on costly auxiliary training. Deviating from that, we here propose a novel steering approach that extracts visual concept directions directly from the image-side activations of Diffusion Transformers. Specifically, we showcase few-shot concept extraction in the activation space using a simple difference-of-means estimator over intermediate residuals. We observe (a) scene-level concepts such as lighting, weather, and style are distributed across image tokens, as well as (b) local concepts such as object colors, textures, materials, and facial attributes are concentrated in specific regions. Towards controlling both concepts, we introduce a new unified training-free framework that uses global difference-of-means for (a) distributed concepts and masked difference-of-means for (b) local concepts, preventing local signals from being diluted by global averaging. Notably, using only a handful of positive and negative prompt pairs, our method identifies and extracts reusable concept directions that can be injected at inference for continuous steering. Quantitatively, our method outperforms text-encoder steering and training-free activation-editing baselines, as well as is competitive with specialized editing models. Our results suggest that as concept directions can be applied at patch level, our method enables precise targeted and compositional steering, manipulating multiple concepts in the same image.

title_en: Prepare Lighter and Faster for Open-Vocabulary Queries: A Query-Wise 3D Segmenter for Gaussian Splatting
abstract_en: Open-vocabulary 3D understanding aims to localize and segment arbitrary objects beyond predefined categories. However, existing approaches based on Gaussian Splatting often rely on expensive preprocessing and lengthy training, limiting their applicability when fast and lightweight solutions are desired. Instead of conventional mask-wise CLIP embeddings, we use dense pixel-level CLIP features to preserve fine-grained semantic information and enable flexible text-driven localization without relying on predefined instance proposals. We then lift the resulting 2D tracklets to 3D Gaussians through a novel visibility voting strategy, yielding accurate 3D segmentation masks with clean object boundaries. title_en: Memorization Lives in a Few Attention Heads: Mitigating Memorization in Diffusion Models via Projection-Based Suppression
abstract_en: Diffusion models can memorize and reproduce training samples during inference, raising serious privacy and copyright concerns. Existing inference-time mitigation methods often suppress conditional information globally, which may reduce memorization but can also harm semantic alignment and image quality. In this paper, we revisit memorization from the perspective of cross-attention heads. Through systematic analysis and targeted ablation, we find that memorization is mainly driven by a small subset of shallow-layer attention heads with abnormally strong semantic control, rather than by the entire cross-attention mechanism. Motivated by this finding, we propose Projection-based Top-k Attention Head Suppression, a targeted inference-time mitigation method. Our method first identifies the top-k attention heads most related to memorization using a semantic-control score, and then removes their condition-specific components through directional projection between conditional and unconditional representations. This design selectively weakens memorization-related features while preserving useful semantic information. Extensive experiments on different diffusion models and datasets show that our method effectively reduces memorization and achieves a better trade-off between memorization mitigation and image quality than existing approaches.

title_en: Pixel-KWS: Rendered-Glyph Representations for Orthographically Robust Open-Vocabulary Keyword Spotting
abstract_en: Open-vocabulary keyword spotting (KWS) allows users to enroll arbitrary keywords at inference time. However, character and phoneme-based text encoders rely on fixed symbol vocabularies learned during training, limiting their ability to handle unseen or visually similar symbols such as homoglyphs, l33tspeak substitutions, and accented characters. We propose PIXEL-KWS, an open-vocabulary KWS framework that represents characters through rendered glyphs rather than learned embedding lookups. We render each character as a grayscale image and encode it with a lightweight CNN, enabling the text encoder to generalize from visual form rather than a fixed vocabulary. On LibriPhrase, PIXEL-KWS and its matched character-based counterpart achieve 9.57% and 9.55% EER on LibriPhrase-hard, 0.43% and 0.41% EER on LibriPhrase-easy, outperforming all published baselines without pre-training or synthetic data. PIXEL-KWS provides substantially greater robustness to both homoglyph and l33tspeak symbol-level perturbations. These results highlight glyph-based representations as a simple and effective approach for robust open-vocabulary KWS in practical settings.

title_en: SARGO: Agreement-Gated Reinforcement and Suppression via On-Policy Self-Guidance for Visual Hallucination Mitigation
abstract_en: Vision-language models remain susceptible to visual hallucinations, often mixing grounded information with unsupported claims in the same response. Response-level reinforcement learning assigns a shared advantage to all tokens in a response, causing negative updates to suppress correct information alongside unsupported claims. To reduce hallucination while preserving useful visual information, we introduce SARGO (Self-guided Advantage-Routed Grounding Optimization), a post-training framework for selective reinforcement and suppression through on-policy self-guidance. Direct and reciprocal weighting gives better-supported tokens stronger reinforcement on positive updates and weaker penalties on negative updates. Agreement between overall and hallucination-specific advantages selects when to apply this guidance. At the response level, a reference-calibrated reward couples factuality with the retention and expansion of grounded information, discouraging lower hallucination scores obtained through omission. Experiments on Qwen3-VL-4B, Qwen3-VL-8B, and Gemma3-4B demonstrate that SARGO outperforms the evaluated mitigation baselines across Obj-Hal, AMBER, THRONE, and SHR evaluations. SARGO achieves these gains while preserving useful visual information and general multimodal capabilities.

title_en: Test-Time Constraint-Aware Diffusion Predictive Control
abstract_en: Diffusion models can learn multimodal distributions over finite-horizon state-input sequences, providing a way to generate candidates for predictive control. However, sequences generated by a pretrained model may violate safety constraints introduced at deployment, for example when obstacles are added or repositioned. Retraining whenever these constraints change limits the usefulness of learned predictive controllers. In this paper, we propose Test-Time Constraint-Aware Diffusion Predictive Control (TCA-DPC), an algorithm for adapting the sampling distribution of a pretrained diffusion controller to newly introduced safety constraints without retraining. We treat the pretrained model as a prior over finite-horizon sequences and define an adapted distribution through exponential tilting based on a constraint-violation penalty. The tilt strength is adjusted online using the fraction of generated sequences that fail constraint verification. We approximately sample the adapted distribution using the Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm in the Gaussian noise space of the pretrained diffusion sampler.

title_en: $β$-number and Its Applications to Data Science
abstract_en: In this paper, we introduce a novel metric, $β$-number, designed to measure the "$p$-th order $d$-dimensional oscillation degree" of a set. For a given set $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, $β$-number is computed by identifying an optimal $d$-dimensional plane $L$ that minimizes the average $p$-th order distance of all points in $K$ to $L$. This metric serves as a versatile tool in data science, functioning both as a dimensionality reduction technique to find the optimal $p$-th order $d$-dimensional subspace and as a measure to characterize data oscillation for classification. We conduct a thorough exploration of $β$-number through theoretical analysis and numerical experiments. Initially, we establish the upper and lower bounds of $β$-number for any set $K$, along with its scaling law. We then elucidate the relationships between $β$-number and its related parameters. A key finding of this study is that in discrete settings, when $p=2$, the $d$-dimensional plane determined by $β$-number coincides with that obtained via Principal Component Analysis (PCA), positioning $β$-number as a generalization of PCA. Furthermore, we propose two algorithms for calculating $β$-number in both continuous and discrete settings. We validate our theoretical results through a series of numerical experiments in low-dimensional cases. Finally, we demonstrate the potential of $β$-number in practical data analysis through a dimensionality reduction task and an image classification task.

title_en: RETR: A Structure-Preserving RGB-Event Transformer for Robust 3D Lane Detection
abstract_en: Robust 3D lane detection requires accurate metric road geometry recovery from visual inputs, yet conventional RGB-based approaches suffer from fragile lane evidence under adverse illumination, motion blur, and long-range perspective compression. Event cameras offer complementary high-temporal-resolution, high dynamic-range structural cues that are robust to these challenges, but their sparse, motion-dependent responses cannot be directly fused into consistent 3D geometry. In this paper, we present the first attempt to introduce event cameras into 3D lane detection. To enable systematic research, we first build two multimodal benchmarks with metric 3D lane annotations: DSEC-3DLD (real-world sequences) and Ev-OpenLane (large-scale simulated sequences). We further propose RETR, a structure preserving transformer that converts complementary RGB and event observations into coherent 3D lane geometry. RETR first aligns modality consistent evidence through Reciprocal Context Flow Fusion, then preserves thin and uncertain lane structures with Uncertainty Aware Structural Consolidation, and finally decodes ordered lane hypotheses using a Geometry State Decoder with proposal conditioned initialization, reference conditioned query evolution, and diversified geometric inquiry. Extensive experiments show that RETR achieves state-of-the-art performance on both benchmarks, especially showing strong improvements in challenging lighting and complex road geometry scenarios. Code and dataset will be available at https://github.com/duskswell/RETR.

title_en: HongguoTrending: A Longitudinal, Multimodal Archive of Trending Videos and Topics on a Leading Micro-Drama Platform
abstract_en: Micro-dramas (duanju) are reshaping digital production and consumption, yet a lack of longitudinal data connecting series to their platform visibility persists, limiting our understanding of the emerging medium. We introduce HongguoTrending, a longitudinal, multimodal dataset of hourly snapshots from seven trending lists of Hongguo, China's largest micro-drama platform. Collected through a two-stage asynchronous pipeline, the archive links 63,200 ranking entries across 632 web list-hours and 157 client hours (889 distinct series) to metadata, cover images, sampled episode videos, and audience engagement metrics. Exploratory analyses show distinct turnover rates between web and mobile trending lists, production-driven mainstream values alongside kinship-centered synopses, genre-specific cover palettes, and strong associations between user sharing and next-day rank gains. Accessible via a RESTful API, this dataset supports empirical research on algorithmic gatekeeping, popularity dynamics, and multimodal digital culture.

title_en: Beyond Alignment: Supervising the Generator for EEG-to-Image Reconstruction
abstract_en: Visual brain decoding translates neural activity into human-interpretable images. While recent EEG-to-image reconstruction methods rely on aligning EEG signals with pretrained visual embeddings to condition an image generator, we empirically demonstrate that stronger cross-modal alignment do not translate into comparable gains in reconstruction quality. This indicates that improving the input condition alone is insufficient; the generative process itself requires explicit supervision. Although Representation Alignment (REPA) offers a solution by guiding diffusion transformers with pretrained vision encoder features, we find that EEG-conditioned generators struggle to follow these fixed targets. To address this mismatch, we introduce generation-derived supervision (GDS): an image-conditioned teacher that translates static image-encoder features into the internal representation space of a diffusion transformer. Our EEG-conditioned student generator closely tracks these dynamic targets during denoising, discarding the teacher at inference. Evaluated on THINGS-EEG and THINGS-MEG, our approach consistently outperforms conditioning-centric baselines, achieving state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity.

title_en: Generate, Align, and Restore: MLLM-Empowered Diffusion for Generalizable Low-light Image Enhancement
abstract_en: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) is essential to numerous vision applications operating under adverse illumination. Despite substantial advances, real-world nighttime enhancement remains challenging due to the scarcity of strictly aligned day-night pairs and complex degradations involving extreme darkness and heterogeneous artificial light sources, leading to fragile generalization. To overcome these challenges, we propose MrLIE (MLLM-empowered reference Low-light Image Enhancement), a novel reference-based unsupervised LLIE framework that synergizes the generative and reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with conditional diffusion. MrLIE employs the MLLM as a high-fidelity reference synthesizer and diagnostic critic, iteratively generating, diagnosing, and correcting normal-light references directly from degraded nighttime observations. Based on this, our method governs the enhancement process through two complementary mechanisms, in which a confidence offset module rectifies spatial-geometric inconsistencies for reference reliability and a structure-anchored injection scheme harmonizes aligned reference cues, low-light structural constraints, and ControlNet additive anchoring during the denoising process. Extensive experiments on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that MrLIE achieves superior perceptual quality, natural appearance, and robust generalization.

title_en: dit.xpu : Taming DiT Sparse Inference on Mobile SoCs
abstract_en: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) enable on-device image generation and editing but incur high attention costs at high resolutions. Existing sparse attention reduces computation, yet dynamic sparsity introduces preprocessing and irregular data accesses that poorly fit mobile NPUs. We present DiT.XPU, a sparse DiT inference framework for heterogeneous mobile SoCs. DiT.XPU combines tile-aligned sparse attention with anchor-based error compensation by exploiting slowly varying dense-sparse output residuals across denoising steps. Heterogeneous XPU collaboration overlaps NPU dense attention with GPU sparse calibration, while mask-guided dataflow reduces data transfers and layout conversion by overlapping data movement with computation. Across five DiT models on two Snapdragon smartphones, DiT.XPU achieves up to 1.56x end-to-end denoising speedup over the Hexagon-NPU backend and 11.5x attention-kernel speedup over the fastest alternative, while preserving generation quality close to dense attention. Code is available at https://github.com/IF-LAB-PKU/dit.xpu.

title_en: Neural Dual Bounds: Valid-by-Construction JGLP Warm-Starts for MAP and Constrained MAP
abstract_en: We present Neural Dual Bounds, a calibration-free framework that produces deterministic upper bounds for MAP inference in probabilistic graphical models using a single neural-network forward pass. The framework trains a network to output the edge messages of a mini-bucket style upper bound on a given join-graph decomposition in a self-supervised manner by directly minimizing a smooth dual objective. The output of this network can be used at test time to warm-start a standard JGLP optimizer. Across diverse benchmarks, this warm start yields dual gaps that are orders of magnitude tighter than those from zero initialization, with the largest gains in the early-iteration regime. We also apply our framework for the constrained MAP (CMPE) task, where neural warm starts with test-time adaptation are comparable to the adaptive baseline on Bayesian networks and achieve the tightest dual gaps, by one to two orders of magnitude, on the grid and segmentation families.

title_en: Zero-shot diffusion image compression with sectioned codebooks and one channel code
abstract_en: Zero-shot diffusion codecs such as Turbo-DDCM compress images without any training. In each coded step, the encoder selects noise vectors from one codebook and transmits a single index for the selected set. We propose sectioned codebooks. A coded step is divided into sections, and each section has its own large codebook and transmits its best vector as a short field of bits. A model based on order statistics quantifies how well the bits of a step are used and predicts the gain of sectioned codebooks from measurements of Turbo-DDCM alone. Fast Walsh-Hadamard transforms make sections of $2^{20}$ vectors practical. At equal bits, sectioned codebooks improve the PSNR of Turbo-DDCM by 0.18 to 0.51 dB on three datasets, improve LPIPS and DISTS, and save 16 to 21% of the bits at equal PSNR. Codecs that are robust to channel errors by design are usually compared only with unprotected codecs. We compare them, at equal total bits, with a codec protected by one channel code. With one BCH code, the sectioned codec outperforms all reported results of Robust Turbo-DDCM and BitFlat on two datasets, by up to 7.74 dB at the highest bit error rate. At the lowest bit error rate its margin over BitFlat is only 0.08 to 0.16 dB. When the code fails, the receiver can still decode the fields as received. Additional experiments cover burst errors and packet loss, and all observed gains of robust codecs stay within a limit derived from the channel capacity.

title_en: Calibrating the Uncertainty of Self-Supervised Monocular Depth without Labels
abstract_en: Self-supervised monocular depth networks can predict a per-pixel uncertainty, which is mainly evaluated by how well it ranks pixels according to their error. Such metrics are insensitive to the magnitude of the uncertainty, so an uncertainty half as large as the actual error obtains the same score. In this paper, we investigate whether the predicted uncertainty is as large as the depth error, both on average (scale) and across confident and uncertain, near and far pixels (shape). On KITTI, the scale is miscalibrated for every uncertainty estimate we evaluate, and the error of MonoProb is nearly twice its predicted uncertainty. We propose MonoCal, which corrects both the scale and the shape without ground-truth depth. Scale calibration multiplies the uncertainty by a single constant measured from stereo pairs, requiring no retraining, and this constant closely matches the one fitted with ground truth. Since a constant cannot change the shape, we further retrain the uncertainty to predict where the depth of the network disagrees with that of a second self-supervised network. Experiments on KITTI show that MonoCal achieves better calibration across uncertainty levels and depth ranges than rescaling with ground truth, while still using a single image at inference. Code will be made publicly available.

title_en: EviRef: Evidence-Specific Memories for Logical Anomaly Detection across Capture Conditions
abstract_en: Logical anomalies arise when every component looks normal but their combination violates the scene rules. In practical inspection, these rules must hold under varying backgrounds, illumination, and imaging quality, with only a few dozen normal images per scene, whereas existing methods couple normality with appearance and merge different constraints into one reference. We model logical normality as decomposable constraints and propose EviRef, a training-free method that builds a separate reference memory for each family of evidence. Component prototypes built once per scene parse images under any capture condition into one label space, on which occupancy and relation constraints are verified. Semantic constraints are verified with whole-image embeddings independent of parsing, and additional evidence such as text is admitted through a task-level gate without modifying existing memories. On VID-AD, EviRef attains a mean image-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 92.1% (88.9% with visual evidence alone), the highest among the compared methods under each of five capture conditions, with a standard deviation of 0.5. Even with memories built from only 20 normal images per task, it surpasses all compared methods that use 50 normal images per task.

title_en: From zero-target transfer to target-site personalization: multi-source training across fall-detection models
abstract_en: Video-based fall detection could support timely assistance when a person cannot call for help. Unfamiliar cameras and scarce local labels challenge deployment. We examine whether joint training improves cross-dataset detection and subsequent local training. We analyze 2,697 clips from eight OmniFall datasets and one AI-Hub dataset. Positive clips contain a fall or collapse transition, while negative clips do not. We hold out each dataset in turn, training on the other eight. We evaluate three vision-language models (VLMs), Qwen, LLaVA, and InternVL, and three visual baselines, CLIP-temporal, VideoMAE, and Pose-TCN. We evaluate the stored source model without target data for training or selection. For each label budget, we update a separate copy using labeled clips from the held-out target dataset. We call this target-site personalization. We compare the Source-initialized model with Target-only, which skips source training but uses identical target clips and updates. Across nine targets, source training raises mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) from frozen-model values of 0.821 to 0.912 for Qwen, 0.883 to 0.947 for LLaVA, and 0.939 to 0.962 for InternVL. With five target examples per class and 26 updates per run, 95% confidence intervals for the AUROC benefit over Target-only lie above zero for Qwen, CLIP-temporal, VideoMAE, and Pose-TCN. With full-target training, they lie above zero only for Qwen and LLaVA. Separate VLM analyses reveal threshold sensitivity and post-fall false detections. The benefit varies by model and label budget.

title_en: DecoEdit: Beyond Flat Control for 3D-Aware Unified Image Editing
abstract_en: While recent advances in multimodal image editing have achieved impressive results, current frameworks remain largely confined to ``flat" 2D controls (e.g., text prompts, bounding boxes, or masks). Precise 3D-aware geometric manipulation -- such as coordinating an object's location, physical scale, and 3D orientation while strictly preserving its fine-grained identity -- remains an elusive challenge, typically suffering from severe detail degradation or requiring expensive per-instance fine-tuning. In this paper, we present DecoEdit, an all-in-one image editing framework that goes beyond flat control by seamlessly integrating 1D textual, 2D spatial, and 3D volumetric inputs under a unified architecture. First, to power this unified model, we establish a data curation pipeline and curate a large-scale dataset, namely DecoDataset, containing 1.6 million samples, encompassing diverse multi-dimensional (1D/2D/3D) tasks and their complex compositions. Furthermore, we establish a comprehensive image editing benchmark named DecoBench to systematically evaluate multi-task editing performance. Finally, to address the fundamental trade-off between complex spatial transformations and identity preservation, we propose a novel decoupled pipeline: DecoEdit factorizes the editing process by utilizing structural guidance from SAM-3D to anchor the target geometry, scale, and spatial orientation, while concurrently leveraging a detail-preservation path to lock in high-fidelity textures. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DecoEdit achieves state-of-the-art results. Notably, on the challenging 3D spatial pose and orientation control tasks, DecoEdit significantly outperforms leading closed-source models such as Seedream 5.0 in both geometric accuracy and identity consistency.

title_en: Puzzle: One Pass Is Not Enough for Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Segmentation
abstract_en: Open-vocabulary remote sensing image segmentation (OVRSIS) enables the segmentation of unseen classes without additional annotation or retraining. By analyzing the predictions of existing OVRSIS methods, we find that many misclassified patches coexist with visually similar, correctly classified patches of the same class within the same image. Unfortunately, most of these methods stop after a single inference rather than using their predictions to guide further inference. Motivated by this observation, we propose \textbf{Puzzle}, a plug-and-play iterative re-inference framework that combines prediction history with a visual-similarity prior to progressively refine patch-level attention. Puzzle employs a lightweight history-conditioned controller to regulate each patch's contribution as an information source and its reliance on visually similar patches, while an adaptive stopping rule determines when to stop. It keeps the segmentation model frozen and reuses the same controller across different models and datasets without retraining. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent performance improvements across diverse OVRSIS models and datasets, highlighting the strong transferability of Puzzle. Moreover, Puzzle can further improve the performance of SOTA methods.

title_en: ST-GAT: A Leakage-Free Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Framework for Robust Network Intrusion Detection
abstract_en: Intrusion detection systems are a central defence in modern networks. Deep learning models report strong anomaly-detection results, but evaluations on standard benchmarks such as CSE-CIC-IDS-2018 are often inflated by two methodological problems: temporal leakage from overlapping sliding windows, and contamination from preprocessing fitted before the train/test split. Per-flow classifiers also ignore the spatio-temporal dependencies across sequences of network flows. We propose a Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Network (ST-GAT) that represents traffic as a sequence of graph snapshots. It builds k-Nearest Neighbour (k-NN) edges within each window, applies multi-head Graph Attention Network (GAT) layers for spatial aggregation, and uses a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network with temporal attention for sequence modelling. To prevent leakage, we use non-overlapping temporal windows (stride equal to window length) and fit all preprocessing on the training split only. We compare three class-imbalance strategies: inverse class-frequency weighting, dynamic balanced sampling, and few-shot metric prototyping. Across three random seeds, ST-GAT with inverse class weighting reached a Macro-F1 of 96.65% (+/- 0.87) and an accuracy of 99.14%. This is 14.3 percentage points higher in Macro-F1 than a per-flow Random Forest baseline (82.34%). Balanced sampling reduced Macro-F1 by 2.3 points (to 94.37%) relative to loss weighting. This suggests that aggressive resampling of small, noisy minority classes can hurt detection in heavily imbalanced traffic.

title_en: CONTEXT-PCa: Evaluating the role of clinical context in MRI-based AI for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (study protocol)
abstract_en: The objective of this study is to investigate the role of clinical variables - their breadth, source, and quality - in the development, utility, and generalisability of an AI system for bi-parametric MRI (bpMRI)-based diagnosis of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa). Clinical context is added to the published PI-CAI-2B image-only model, whose weights are fixed. The study cohort comprises 6,022 biparametric MRI cases from 4,540 patients at University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (2019-2024), of which 4,834 cases (3,632 patients) are held out for internal testing. Forty-three clinical variables are drawn from structured health records, clinical letters, MRI reports, and automated image measurements. The primary endpoint is the difference in the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) between the image-context and image-only models on the internal test set. Secondary analyses compare combining strategies, the contribution of individual variables, and performance across subgroups. All models are further tested on five external cohorts from primary diagnosis and population-based screening.
